_: The sketch of 25 November 2026 over the 70-76 Riley Street study: each neighbour's tower on the outline drawn, at the storeys written in its middle and the setbacks written on its sides (where a side has no figure, as drawn, measured off the sketch at 1:1 against our lot); no podiums are drawn, so each tower stands on a three-storey podium over its whole lot. See the density file for the keys. Every scenario takes away 88-108 and 72-80 William St (a scenario's `removed`, by address, takes a building out of the plan, the massing and the sun study). Steps 1 to 5, marked up on 25 November, read the sketch down a step at a time: the sketch itself; Crown St north a 7-storey podium; 54-64 Riley St one too; 67-89 Riley St at 14 storeys; every block at 7 storeys, a four-storey podium and three storeys 3 m off the long streets.

scenarios.lead: Every block round us is built to 7 storeys, the 23.4 m height of building: across Riley Street, 67-107 Riley St as one site; north of us, 54-68 Riley St with 1 Crown Lane, 66-68 Riley St with them; across Crown Lane, the whole Crown Street block, 89 to 129 Crown St with 4 and 10 Crown Lane. Each is a four-storey podium over its lot and three storeys above it, held 3 m off its two long street frontages. The William Street towers are taken away, as in every scenario; 109 Riley St, the former hotel, is a heritage item (I436) and stays. Ours is built the same way: a four-storey podium over our lot and three storeys above it, 6 m off our northern boundary and 3 m off Riley Street, Crown Lane and Stanley Lane, 7 storeys in all.
